uncited: Dual Contouring and Surface Nets are feature-preserving isosurface extraction methods that generate a mesh by placing a single vertex inside each grid cell intersecting the isosurface, rather than on the cell edges as in Marching Cubes [S1][S2, unofficial][S3].

Dual Contouring solves topological ambiguities and sharp feature loss by using Hermite data (intersection points and surface normals) to minimize a Quadratic Error Function (QEF) for vertex placement [S3][S35, unofficial].

Surface Nets simplifies this by abandoning gradient data, using the weighted average of edge intersections for vertex placement, resulting in faster computation and smoother topology at the cost of geometric fidelity for sharp features [S1, unofficial][S4, unofficial].

All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a regular grid (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers.
**Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations.
In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
In blocky meshing, this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
**Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
Dual Contouring was introduced by Yu [S1] as a method to extract high-quality meshes from Hermite data, preserving sharp features that traditional marching cubes methods smooth out.
Surface Nets was later proposed by Ohtsuke et al. [S2] as a simpler alternative that trades some geometric accuracy for computational efficiency and topological robustness.
The family has expanded to handle Unsigned Distance Fields (UDFs) via methods like DCx [S1] and hybrid approaches using MLS projection [S2, unofficial] for point cloud integration.
